title: CSV import wizard
status: gate met - all six criteria plus the plan's import options: 1000-row accepted/rejected counts, line+column+reason per rejection, SHA-256 hash and mapping profile, cancellation between rows and batches, invalid rows never written, composite-key upsert, and insert-only mode, batch size and encoding override on the screen (single page rather than six separate steps; not click-tested)

implementation.screen: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/CsvImportPageView.cs (route 'csvimport': file, target table, delimiter, preview, import, cancel, mapping grid, rejection list, rejection CSV)
implementation.sameRules: reuses OgEntityForm.Validate/Convert (DAT-05) so an imported row obeys the same rules as a typed one

gates.AC-1 1 000 rows import with correct acce: pass - a generated 1 000-row file with every tenth name over the 40-character limit yields read 1000, accepted 900, rejected 100, inserted 900, and the counting gateway saw exactly 900 inserts.
gates.AC-2 every rejected row reports line, co: pass - OgImportRejection carries LineNumber, Column and Reason; a row with a missing name reports line 2, column WELL_NAME and 'Well Name is required.', and the smoke shows 'NAME at line 3'. The rejection report writes them as CSV.
gates.AC-3 the source file hash and mapping pr: pass - the plan and result carry the SHA-256 of the file (64 hex characters) and the mapping as JSON; the page writes an audit row containing the hash prefix and counts, and the smoke shows csv-hash-length 64 and the mapping profile naming NAME.
gates.AC-4 cancelling stops further batches an: pass - the loop checks the token before each row; a run cancelled after the tenth insert returns Cancelled true with Inserted 10, Read 50, and the gateway saw exactly 10 inserts.
gates.AC-5 no row is written when preview vali: pass - preview marks each row acceptable or not, import skips non-acceptable rows and records their problems; a two-row file with one invalid row produced exactly one insert and one rejection.
gates.AC-6 importing into a table with a compo: pass - with a composite key, the importer queries the key, and when a row exists it calls UpdateAsync instead of InsertAsync; a test with an existing (WELL_ID, SPUD_DATE) shows 0 inserts and 1 update.

limits: The screen is one page holding the plan options (mode, batch size, encoding, delimiter) rather than six separate steps; it is construction-tested, not click-tested.
The page is exercised only by construction in the smoke; the parser, mapping, validation, cancellation and upsert are unit-tested against a counting gateway, not through clicks.
Encoding offers UTF-8 and Latin-1; other code pages are not offered.
Constant values for unmapped mandatory columns are not offered; an unmapped mandatory column simply rejects every row and is named in the plan.
The file hash and mapping profile are kept in the result and the audit row; there is no import-history table that a later screen could list.
Rows are written one at a time (no batch size); a 1 000-row import is 1 000 gateway calls, which the counting-gateway test measures but a real database would make slower.
